title: Human-in-the-loop follow-through: request changes, retry from a run, decisions on the trace, one vocabulary
findings: Rejecting an action discards the whole run, the approver's note never reaches the agent, and an action cannot be edited before approval
A failed run's trace offers no next step: no retry, and skipped schedule occurrences leave no trace
Approval decisions are write-only: who approved and why is never shown in the trace, the API or the audit detail
One request is described with three nouns (task, goal, run) across four overlapping 'what is happening' screens
Overlapping work screens and three names for one action make the product harder to learn than it needs to be
spec:
Rules: the standard rules apply. 'Edit and approve' is out of scope: it needs mcp-core schema and policy re-evaluation, and that area is excluded. No migration is needed.

1) Request changes (send back with feedback)
- DecisionRequest gains mode: approve, reject or request_changes. When mode is missing, derive it from `approved`.
- request_changes requires a note. In one transaction:
  - set the approval status to 'rejected', with detail sentBack=true;
  - claim the run from waiting_approval (claimParked);
  - write a tool_call step for that toolCallId with status REJECTED and modelContent {status: 'rejected', note, instruction: 'Do not repeat this action unchanged. Revise it using the feedback, or explain why you cannot.'};
  - then submitResume.
- rebuildConversation uses the REJECTED step as the tool result. latestApprovalReadyToExecute and answeredAfter accept it.
- After a request-changes in a run, every OUTBOUND or DESTRUCTIVE call in that run requires approval, whatever the grant says.
- Limits: when the same tool is sent back a second time in one run, end the run with 'Stopped after two rounds of requested changes.' Allow at most 2 rounds per run.
- Reject still stops the run. Expiry still cancels it.
- UI (Approvals.tsx and InlineApproval): three actions, each with copy that states its consequence:
  - Approve;
  - 'Send back with feedback' (note required);
  - 'Reject and stop'.

2) Retry from a run
RunDetail shows 'Try again' for failed, abandoned or cancelled runs.
- Goal-backed run: call the goal retry. The confirmation lists the previous attempt's completed actions from the WP11 step metadata.
- Direct run: call the new POST /api/runs/{id}/retry. Allowed for the requester, or holders of the permission used to start runs plus run:cancel. It creates a new direct run with the original instruction through AgentRunner.prepare and drive, and then navigates to the new run.

3) Decisions on the trace
- TraceStep approval steps fetch WP14's GET /api/approvals/{id} using the approvalId in the step detail.
- Show one of: 'Approved by <name> at 10:42', 'Sent back by <name>: <note>', 'Rejected by <name>: <note>', or 'Expired without a decision'.
- Resolve names through the member directory.

4) One vocabulary
- Rename the 'New goal' buttons in Orchestrator.tsx and Board.tsx to 'Give an agent a task'.
- TaskDialog copy talks about the task.
- labels.ts: change 'Goal task:' to 'Task:'.
- GoalSheet and Tasks show the goal layer only for goals with more than one task.
- On the agent page, TaskDialog creates a one-task goal (useCreateGoal with agentId), so the work appears on the board and can be retried and stopped. The direct-run API remains for integrations.

Tests
- Request changes resumes the run with the note in the tool result.
- The two-round cap ends the run.
- A forced approval follows feedback.
- Direct-run retry creates a new run.
- Trace decision rendering.

Acceptance (live)
- On a sandbox email approval, 'Send back with feedback: use a softer tone' produces a new approval with a revised body.
- 'Try again' on a failed run starts a new attempt.
